title: Pan-seared steak
summary: A properly seared steak, the best test of 'too hot / not hot enough'.
source: Starter outline written by Claude. Matthew: replace/compare with a TheMealDB import, then hand-check.
ingredients: 1 sirloin or ribeye steak, ~2.5cm thick, at room temperature
1 tbsp high smoke point oil (vegetable, rapeseed)

steps.instruction: Pat the steak dry with kitchen paper and season well on both sides.
looks_wrong: wet steak straight from the packet (it won't sear)

steps.instruction: Heat a heavy pan on high until very hot, then add the oil.
looks_wrong: heavy smoke (too hot, take it off)
steps.done_when: Oil shimmers and just starts to smoke.

steps.instruction: Lay the steak in, away from you. Don't move it.
looks_right: loud sizzle as it goes in
looks_wrong: steak being poked and moved around
steps.done_when: Steak is in. Start the side-1 timer (3 min for medium-rare).

steps.instruction: Flip the steak. Add the butter, garlic and herbs, and spoon the butter over.
looks_right: deep brown crust on the cooked side
steps.done_when: Second side seared. Check with a thermometer: 57°C for medium-rare.

steps.instruction: Rest the steak on a board for 5 minutes, then slice against the grain.
looks_right: steak resting, not being cut straight away
steps.done_when: Rested and sliced. Ask the cook to show the inside to the camera.
